Since \(A>B>C\), for \(A=1\) there is no possible \(B,C\) with \(C<B<1\).  
For \(A=2\), the only possibility is \(B=1,C=0\). Then the number is \(210DE\), which is automatically less than \(22222\).

Now \(C<D<E\) means \(0<D<E\), so \(D,E\) are two distinct digits from \(1,\dots,9\) in increasing order.

\[
\binom{9}{2}=36
\]

\boxed{36}
